raw:
Let me analyze this task. The user wants me to write strings for a desktop app's uninstaller (English), following the ui-microcopy skill doctrine.

Five strings needed:
- s1: dialog title asking whether to uninstall
- s2: button that performs the uninstall
- s3: button that keeps the app
- s4: status line while files are being removed
- s5: error when uninstall fails because app is still running

The skill is written in zh-TW examples but the output is English. The doctrine is universal though: 
- dialog-title: names the act, noun or verb phrase, no question mark
- button: imperative verb phrase
- status: closed state / in-progress state (動詞＋中)
- error: state, then cause if known, then recovery step if one exists

Key constraints:
- No question marks in dialog titles (rejected: 您確定嗎？、真的要刪除嗎？; accepted: 刪除這筆紀錄、中斷安裝 — "Delete this record", "Abort installation")
- Buttons: imperative verb, conventional labels. The button that cancels should be "Cancel" per Apple/Microsoft guidance — do not rename Cancel while Cancel is unambiguous. The button that keeps the app — it declines the offer / closes without deciding. In an uninstall confirmation dialog, the button that keeps the app is the cancel button. The conventional label is "Cancel". Google/Microsoft/Apple all say keep the Cancel name. Some uninstallers use "Keep" but mainstream guidance in the skill says "always title a cancelling button Cancel". The dialog asks whether to uninstall; the button that keeps the app cancels the uninstall — so "Cancel".

Wait, but the skill also says "declines an offer the app made → 不用了、稍後" — but that's when the label "Cancel" would cancel something else. Here the dialog is a yes/no confirmation; the standard pairing is "Uninstall" / "Cancel". So s3 = "Cancel".

- s2: "Uninstall" — conventional action label.

- s1: dialog title names the act. English convention: "Uninstall App Name" or "Uninstall [App]". Microsoft guidance for uninstall dialogs: title is the app name or "Uninstall". E.g., macOS: "Are you sure you want to uninstall..." — but no question marks per the skill. So "Uninstall" or "Uninstall AppName". Since we don't know the app name, generic: "Uninstall" — maybe "Uninstall the app"? Hmm. The role says "names the act, noun or verb phrase". "Uninstall" as a verb phrase names the act. That's conventional: many uninstallers title the dialog "Uninstall". Keep it short: "Uninstall".

- s4: status while files are being removed: 進行中 form: "Uninstalling…" or "Removing files…". In-progress form uses verb+中 (同步中 = Syncing). English: "Uninstalling…" — with ellipsis for in-progress. Status closed state would be "Uninstall complete". Ongoing: "Uninstalling…" — that's the conventional wording. "Removing files…" is more specific but "Uninstalling…" is the conventional one and short. The skill prefers shortest conventional wording that preserves meaning. "Uninstalling…" is fine. Should the ellipsis be there? In English UI, in-progress often uses "…". The skill says ellipsis form 「……」 for zh; for English "..." typographical ellipsis "…" is standard. Buttons/status: in Material, "Uninstalling…" is used. I'll use "Uninstalling…".

- s5: error when app is still running: state, cause, recovery. "Cannot uninstall: [App] is running. Close the app and try again." Per the format: 無法安裝：這是目前的開機磁碟。請選擇其他磁碟。 → "Cannot uninstall: the app is running. Close it and try again." Or "Uninstall failed: the app is still running. Close the app, then try again."

English convention: "Uninstaller can't remove files while [App] is running. Close [App] and try again." Hmm. Let's follow the error role: state (cannot uninstall), cause (app is running), recovery (close the app, then try again).

"Cannot uninstall: the app is still running. Close the app and try again."

That's clean. The task says "tell the user what to do" — so recovery step is required.

No affect, no apology ("Sorry", "Oops" — none), no exclamation.

The instruction says return only JSON. So output exactly the JSON object with s1–s5.

Let me draft:

s1: "Uninstall" — hmm, as a dialog title asking whether to uninstall. Maybe "Uninstall the app"? Without a known app name, "Uninstall" is the title naming the act. Microsoft style: title = shortest form of the instruction, e.g. "Uninstall app?" — but no question mark allowed. Windows commonly titles it "Uninstall". I'll use "Uninstall".

Actually, the dialog body would carry the consequence, but we're not asked for body text. s1 is just the title: "Uninstall".

s2: "Uninstall"
s3: "Cancel"
s4: "Uninstalling…"
s5: "Cannot uninstall: the app is still running. Close the app and try again."

Check the six tests:
- Deletion: each clause in s5 needed — state, cause, recovery. Yes.
- Counter-question: "the app is still running" — user would ask "why did it fail?" Answered. Fine.
- Visible — fine.
- Chat: none of these are conversational replies. Good.
- Control: buttons name actions. Good.
- Provenance: none.

No trailing periods on buttons/titles; sentence periods on the status/error. s4 "Uninstalling…" — in-progress status, ends with ellipsis which is conventional for in-progress, no full stop after. Fine.

JSON only. Keys s1..s5.

Output:
{"s1":"Uninstall","s2":"Uninstall","s3":"Cancel","s4":"Uninstalling…","s5":"Cannot uninstall: the app is still running. Close the app and try again."}

Should s1 be different from s2? Title "Uninstall" and button "Uninstall" — that's actually the standard Windows pattern (title "Uninstall [Product]", buttons "Uninstall"/"Cancel"). Without a product name they're identical, which is fine and conventional. Alternatively s1 could be "Uninstall the app" — clunky. Keep "Uninstall".

Use the ellipsis character "…" not "...". Yes.{"s1":"Uninstall","s2":"Uninstall","s3":"Cancel","s4":"Uninstalling…","s5":"Cannot uninstall: the app is still running. Close the app and try again."}

parsed.s5: Cannot uninstall: the app is still running. Close the app and try again.
